summary: A 1933 Forest Service steel tower in Natchitoches Parish, Louisiana, retired from fire watch in 1982; the register and a second source disagree on its height and build date.

facts.design: Steel Aermotor LX-25 tower; original ladder replaced with stairs in 1952

staffing.status: no longer used for fire watch

events.note: Built by the U.S. Forest Service, per the register
Original access ladder replaced with stairs
Forest Service fire suppression use ended; state overflights took over the task
Registered February 2, 2011 as US 901, LA 5; nominated by Geoffrey R. Lehmann

evidence.supports: built 1933 by the U.S. Forest Service
evidence.quote: Constructed in 1933 by the U.S. Forest Service

evidence.supports: steel Aermotor LX-25 tower, 99 ft 9 in tall

evidence.quote: Its original access ladder was replaced with stairs in 1952.

evidence.supports: Forest Service fire suppression use until 1982, then state overflights
evidence.quote: The tower was used as part of the Forest Service fire suppression system until 1982 when the task was taken over by State overflights.

evidence.supports: 1934 Forest Service photo on the register page
evidence.quote: 1934 photo - courtesy of U.S. Forest Service

evidence.supports: location in Kisatchie National Forest, Natchitoches Parish
Kisatchie Ranger District is a cooperator
second source: 82-foot steel tower with 7x7 cab erected 1951-52
evidence.quote: 1951 - 52: The Kisatchie National Forest erected a 82-foot steel tower with a 7x7 cab.

evidence.supports: Wikipedia list: still standing and in active use

corrections.why: The register gives the tower as 99 ft 9 in (about 30.4 m). The record's 25.0 m is about 82 feet, the figure given by a second source that conflicts with the register.

sources.title: List of fire lookout towers in Louisiana

notes_for_editor: Unresolved conflict: the register says a 99 ft 9 in Aermotor LX-25 built in 1933 (with a 1934 USFS photo and a 1952 stair change); the central Louisiana lookouts site says an 82-ft steel tower with a 7x7 cab was erected in 1951-52. It may be a replacement or a different tower. The Forest History Society PDF 'A History of Kisatchie' was searched by keyword and did not yield a Kisatchie-tower entry. No source found on current access or climbability; the access level is left out of facts. The Wikipedia 'active use' status is undated. The record's height_m 25.0 conflicts with the register.
